question: Should [profile.max] (fat LTO, codegen-units=1) be the release default? (sheet U-C10)

corpus.note: 51/58 type-check clean under both binaries — behaviour is identical

caveat: Both builds ran under CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 inside a MemoryMax=8G scope (the box's memory-safe recipe), not the repository's configured jobs=8. Absolute build times are inflated and the max/release build-time ratio may shift at 8 jobs. Size and functional behaviour are unaffected.

max.settings: fat LTO, codegen-units=1, no incremental, strip

superseded_first_pass.note: The first pass reported max at 10.225 ms vs release 12.699 ms median (-19.5%) and 30.0 vs 25.7 files/s. THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE on a re-run and is recorded here as a measurement-conditions artifact, not a result. It also used the pre-fix throughput metric, which was --iters-dependent.

verdict.decision: Ship released artifacts with `--profile max` (smaller binary, less RSS). Keep [profile.release] as the dev-iteration profile so ordinary builds are not slowed. Do NOT claim a runtime win — the measurement does not support one.
